verification_note: Telangana is a fully segregated code path. Andhra Pradesh entries must never be substituted here even where the two states inherited a common predecessor statute — post-reorganisation amendments, rules, notifications and portals diverge.

obligations.summary: Shops and commercial establishments operating in the state register with the state labour department.
Working hours, weekly holidays, overtime and leave entitlements are set by state rules and differ from neighbouring states.
Permission conditions for night working, particularly for women employees, are state-notified.

instruments.title: Telangana Tax on Professions, Trades, Callings and Employments Act, 1987
instruments.authority: Commercial Taxes Department, Government of Telangana

obligations.summary: Employer registration and employee enrolment for professional tax are state-specific and do not transfer across state lines.
Periodic deduction and remittance follow the state's own slab notification.
Employer and employee welfare-fund contributions are payable on the state's own cycle.

instruments.title: Telangana rules under the Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) framework

obligations.summary: Engaging contract labour above the state threshold requires principal-employer registration and contractor licensing under state rules.

instruments.title: Telangana State Industrial Project Approval and Self-Certification System (TS-iPASS) framework
instruments.authority: Industries and Commerce Department, Government of Telangana

obligations.summary: Industrial approvals in the state are routed through the state single-window system rather than through central portals.

state_escalation_triggers: Deploying employees across Telangana and another state under one payroll — professional tax, welfare fund and shops-and-establishments registration do not travel across the border.
Relying on a pre-2014 combined Andhra Pradesh precedent without confirming its post-reorganisation status in Telangana.
